headline: Japanese figure skater Mao Shimada wins a second Grand Prix in her debut season

paragraphs.text: HELSINKI, Finland (AP) — Mao Shimada of Japan won the Finlandia Trophy Grand Prix on Saturday, making it two-of-two for the 18-year-old in her first senior-level figure staking season.

Shimada entered the campaign after winning four consecutive junior world titles and has kept up her winning streak in skating’s big league. She won Skate Canada International this month and followed that up with another dominant performance in Helsinki.

Already owning a comfortable lead after her short program on Friday, Shimada ran away with it by shaking off an early fall on a quad toeloop early in her free skate to “Waloyo Yamoni” by Christopher Tin. That gave her a total of 229.49 points for the two-day meet.
Niina Petrokina of Estonia, the reigning European champion, was second with 214.06 total points. American Isabeau Levito was third with 207.19, completing a repeat of the podium at Skate Canada.

Japanese women have won all five Grand Prix events so far this season. Olympic bronze medalist Ami Nakai won the season-opener in France and Skate America last week, while Mone Chiba won the Cup of China earlier this month.
The regular season ends with NHK Trophy in Tokyo next week.

The top six performers in the rankings for each discipline will then qualify for the Grand Prix Final in China from December 10-12. Shimada and Nakai are leading the women’s standings, followed by Alexandra Ignatova, Petrokina and Anastasiia Gubanova. Levito is clinging to sixth and the final berth for the final.
Seven Russian skaters were withdrawn from the meet early this week after the Finnish government barred Russian athletes from entering the country due to the war in Ukraine.
